( GIRISH CHATNI)
XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT

The P.I., of K.R.Puram Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A, 323, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, CW.2 and 3 are being the parents of CW.1 have performed the marriage of the CW.1 on 29.05.2020 with accused No.1 at 'Sri.Shiva Parvathi Kalyana Mantapa', O.M.B.R, Layout, Chikkabanasavadi, Bengaluru in the presence of the elders, at the time of marriage, as per the demand of accused No.2, 3 and 4, CW.2 and 3 have given Rs.1,00,000/- cash, 37 grams gold chain, Ring and Bracelet to the accused No.1 and 120 grams of gold put on CW.1 i.e., Earrings,
Shamili vs Syam Prasanna on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121525759/
2 Jumuki, Necklace, Chain, Bangals C.C.No.56889/2022 and ring as dowry and spend Rs.5,00,000/- to perform the marriage.

It is further alleged that, the complainant went to her matrimonial house and led marital life with accused No.1 at house No.18,
2nd Cross, 2nd Main, P & T Layout, Anandapura, T.C.Palya, K.R.Puram along with accused No.2 to 4, who are the mother, brother and sister-in-law of accused No.1.

It is further alleged that, after 4-5 months, the accused No.1 started to abuse CW.1 in filthy language and demanded an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- from the parents of CW.1 and picked up quarrel with her and subjected her to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally for dowry.

It is further alleged that, on 13.12.2021, accused No.1 to 4 with a common intention picked up quarrel with CW.1 and demanded her to bring dowry from her parental house and abused her in filthy language, and assaulted her by hand and thrown CW.1 from her marital house and subjected her to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally for dowry.

Based on the written complaint lodged by C.W.1, CW.7 has registered the case against accused No.1 to 3 in P.S. Crime No.389/2021 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a), 323, 504,
506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Investigating Officers/ CW.7 and 8 investigated the matter, after completion of the investigation CW.8 has submitted final C.C.No.56889/2022 report against the accused No.1 to 4 for the above said offences.
3. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 4 and registered the criminal case against them.
4. After registering the case, the accused No.1 to 4 have appeared before this court and enlarged on bail as they are obtained anticipatory bail.
Copy of the final report and its' enclosures were furnished to them in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused No.1 to 4.
They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. In order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4, the prosecution has examined one witness out of 08 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and closed its side.

In lieu of absence of incriminating circumstances appearing against accused,
recording of his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.
Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

7. The points that arise for my consideration are;
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, CW.1 got married to accused No.1 on 29.05.2020, after the marriage CW-1 has led marital life at her matrimonial house along with accused No.1 to 4 and subsequently accused No.1 to 4 with a common intention have physically Shamili vs Syam Prasanna on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121525759/
3 and mentally subjected CW.1 to cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 13.12.2021, accused No.1 to 4 with a common intention assaulted CW.1 with hands for more dowry and caused simple injury and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.323 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common C.C.No.56889/2022 intention have abused CW.1 in filthy language and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.504 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused No.1 has demanded Rs.1,00,000/- dowry from CW.1 and accused No.1 to 4 subjected her to cruelty and demanded for more dowry and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?
6. What Order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 to 5 : In the Negative.
 Point No.6 : As per the final order  for the following;
 C.C.No.56889/2022  REASONS  9. POINT NOs.1 AND 5 :-
As these five points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4, the prosecution has examined the complainant/victim/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and relied upon Eight documents.

10. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has examined the complainant / victim CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, the said witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned APP appearing for the State with permission treated the said witness as Shamili vs Syam Prasanna on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121525759/
4 hostile and fully cross examined her, wherein, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 in order to prove the guilt of the accused persons.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. On perusal of the materials on record and the oral & documentary evidence of P.W.1, she has categorically admitted that, she has compromised the matter with the C.C.No.56889/2022 accused persons.

In view of the evidence of P.W.1, since the matter was compromised, the prayer of the learned Senior Asst. Public Prosecutor for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses was rejected as no purpose would be served.
As the P.W.1 has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution, the evidence on record is not at all helpful to substantiate the guilt of the accused persons.
Hence, there is no cogent and convincing evidence against the accused persons.
Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused No.1 to 4 and hence, the Point Nos.1 to 5 are answered in the "Negative".

12. Point No.6 :- In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A, 323, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bonds and Surety bonds of the accused persons shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter C.C.No.56889/2022 it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 05 th day of March, 2025.)
(GIRISH CHATNI)
